facts.value: Full 2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy Statement, MRP Policy and Annual Investment Strategy — 39-page paper, MUFG Corporate Markets template

source.title: TMSS, MRP Policy Statement and Annual Investment Strategy 2026/2027 — Cabinet, 3 February 2026, agenda paper 83284

facts.note: Cabinet recommended to Council. Advisor MUFG Corporate Markets (para 1.5, p.7). Rate forecasts based on MUFG data as at 22 December 2025 (p.15). All treasury figures below cited to page numbers in this single paper — no separate appendix pack.
Walk: 77,772 → 95,502 → 101,350 → 106,591 → 104,445. Total rise £28.8m (37%). Movement heaviest in 2026/27 (+£17,730k). MRP + other movements deducted at £1,184-2,451k per year.

facts.value: £30.332m (2025/26 estimate at 31 March 2026) walking to £64.421m by 31 March 2030 — a 2.12x expansion

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 — Section 3.1 gross debt/CFR table, p.14

facts.note: Walk: 30,332 → 49,400 → 56,850 → 64,116 → 64,421. Additions of £19.1m in 2026/27, then £7.5m, £7.3m, £0.3m. Change tracks the net financing need line on p.8 exactly.

facts.value: Total external borrowing £35.0m at 31.12.25 (PWLB £20.0m 57%, Barclays £10.0m 29%, Local Authorities £5.0m 14%). Treasury investments £13.47m. Net borrower £21.53m.

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 — Section 3.1 current portfolio table, p.13

facts.note: At 31.3.25 the composition was: PWLB £20.0m (unchanged), Barclays £10.0m (unchanged), Local Authorities £8.5m (£3.5m has since rolled off). Investments at 31.3.25 were £17.015m (76% MMF, 24% LAs); at 31.12.25 £13.470m (55% Banks, 45% MMF). PWLB position UNCHANGED at £20.0m across both dates in the paper.

facts.value: £47.440m (2025/26 estimate) — 61% of CFR — walking down modestly to £40.025m by 2029/30

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 — 'BORROWING' row on p.14 gross-debt-vs-CFR table

facts.note: Walk: 47,440 → 46,103 → 44,499 → 42,476 → 40,025. Only £7.4m of internal capacity is consumed over five years while gross external debt more than doubles (+£34.1m). Internal share of CFR falls from 61% to 38%. Verbatim strategy narrative (p.17): 'the Council is currently maintaining an under-borrowed position...cash supporting the Council's reserves, balances and cash flow has been used as a temporary measure.'

facts.value: £0 in main tables; £1.0m headroom in Operational Boundary and Authorised Limit (flat across five years)

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 — Operational Boundary and Authorised Limit tables, p.14

facts.note: The paper does not print a specific OLTL figure in the CFR or gross-debt tables. IFRS 16 lease policy discussed at Section 2.6 (p.10-11), applied retrospectively. Balance-sheet identity treats OLTL as £0 (matches the paper's own arithmetic on p.14).

facts.value: CFR − External debt − OLTL = Internal borrowing. TIES across all five years to £1k rounding.
£25m of fixed-rate borrowing sits in the under-12-month bucket (2025/26 reference position)

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 — Appendix 5.1.3 maturity structure table, p.30

facts.note: The table shows £25m under 12 months and £0 in every other maturity bucket (12m-2yr, 2yr-50yr, 50yr+). Against total external debt of £30.3m at 31.3.26 (p.14) — so essentially the whole fixed book is short-dated. Consistent with p.13 showing PWLB £20m, Barclays £10m and £5m LA at 31.12.25. Upper limits on fixed net debt 100%, variable 40%.

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 — Section 2.1 and Appendix 5.1.1, pp.8 and 29

facts.note: 2026/27 is the pivotal year at £70.4m (nearly double 2025/26's £40.3m). Financing sources for 2026/27: Capital Receipts £23.9m, Capital Grants £16.5m, Reserves £5.9m, Unsupported Borrowing £3.3m. Net financing need £19.07m — the single largest draw in the five-year plan.

Unusual profile — the 2026/27 peak (7.30%) and 2027/28 trough (3.90%) sit against the £19.07m net financing need spike and £7.45m follow-through. Most councils in the library show smoother walks. The paper does not print a footnote explaining the 3.90% dip.

facts.value: £84m (2025/26) rising to £113m (2028/29), easing to £111m (2029/30) — Debt component alone £83m→£112m→£110m; OLTL £1m flat throughout

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 — Section 3.2, Operational Boundary table, p.14

facts.note: Substantial headroom against the £30-64m gross debt path (roughly £53-49m of unused Operational Boundary throughout). Not the binding constraint.

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 — Section 3.2, Authorised Limit table, p.14

facts.note: Statutory ceiling under s.3(1) Local Government Act 2003. Above the Operational Boundary by £10m across every year.

facts.value: Four LB components enumerated in Section 2.3 (p.9); NO CHART AND NO NUMBERS printed for the liability benchmark itself

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 — Section 2.3 liability benchmark narrative, p.9

facts.note: Paper lists the four components (existing loan debt outstanding, Loans CFR, Net loans requirement, Liability benchmark = gross loans requirement) but publishes no LB chart or numeric pathway. Code requires estimation for at least the current year plus two more. Missing detail worth flagging softly — most district strategies in the library carry a printed LB pathway.

facts.value: MUFG 22.12.25: Bank Rate 3.75% Mar-26 falling to 3.25% by Dec-26 and held through Mar-29. 5yr PWLB 4.60% Mar-26 falling to 4.10% by Mar-27. Current (22.12.25 pm) certainty rates 5y 4.81%, 10y 5.39%, 25y 6.01%, 50y 5.78%; target end Q4 2027 5y 4.10%, 10y 4.70%, 25y 5.30%, 50y 5.10%.
facts.note: Verbatim borrowing advice (p.16): 'better value can be obtained at the shorter end of the curve (<5 years PWLB maturity/<10 years PWLB EIP) and short-dated fixed rates should also be considered.' MUFG's long-run Bank Rate neutral remains 3.5%. Report expects rate cut Q2 2026 to 3.5% then Q4 2026 to 3.25%.

facts.value: Under-borrowed position maintained. Contingent responses: postpone if sharp rise risk; draw fixed rate now if sharper fall risk.
facts.note: Verbatim: 'medium and longer dated borrowing rates are expected to fall from their current levels, albeit only once prevailing inflation concerns are addressed by restrictive near-term monetary policy.' Rescheduling considered 'whilst premature redemption rates remain elevated but only if there is surplus cash available' (Section 3.6, p.18).

facts.value: Priorities Security→Liquidity→Yield. Non-specified investment cap £4m; LA counterparty cap £10m; wholly-owned company cap £12m; non-UK country cap £4m. Investment earnings forecast (MUFG 22.12.25): 3.80% residual 25/26, 3.40% 26/27, 3.30% 27/28-28/29, 3.50% 29/30.
facts.note: No investments >365 days at 31.12.25 (§4.3, p.26). Benchmark 7-day to 12-month SONIA. All counterparties within MUFG creditworthiness colour bands. Credit criteria unchanged from prior year.

facts.value: Asset life method for Capitalisation Direction expenditure. From April 2025, cannot exclude any amount of CFR from prudent MRP calculation (Reg 27 amendment). MRP begins financial year following asset availability. IFRS 16 leases treated retrospectively with catch-up in first year.
facts.note: MRP charge deducted from CFR walks at £1,184k → £1,337k → £1,603k → £2,024k → £2,451k across the five years (from Section 2.2 CFR table, p.9). VRP disclosure required at Section 2.9. Nothing distressed in the policy statement.

signals.headline: Gross external debt more than doubles from £30.3m to £64.4m over four years while internal borrowing runs down only £47.4m to £40.0m — most new capital funded externally, not from internal capacity
signals.why_it_matters: The forward borrowing profile concentrates the treasury decisions of the next 2-3 years into a rate call. Strategy states expectation that rates fall (p.17), consistent with the under-borrowed stance, but £25m of fixed debt already sits under 12 months so significant drawings must be arranged regardless.

signals.headline: £25m of £30m external debt sits in the under-12-month maturity bucket (p.30); combined with £34m of planned additions to 2029/30, ~£59m of gross new borrowing to organise
signals.why_it_matters: Not gradual laddered rolls of a smooth book — the entire fixed portfolio is concentrated in the near bucket. Rollover timing decisions dominate the strategy over the next 12-24 months.

signals.headline: TMSS 2026/27 approved £70.4m capital programme with £19.07m net financing need — largest single-year draw in the five-year plan
signals.why_it_matters: The step-change in capital spend in 2026/27 is the immediate driver of the £34m of gross debt additions across the plan. Cabinet 3 Feb 2026 recommended to Council for approval.

officer.body:
Dear [OFFICER],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are some thoughts on the 2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy taken to Cabinet on 3 February. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. The strategy is coherent and the MUFG template is followed cleanly, so this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

The shape that jumped out is on the forward borrowing profile. The prudential indicator on page 14 walks actual gross debt from £30.3m at 31 March 2026 to £64.4m by 31 March 2030 — a doubling in four years. And the maturity structure of your fixed borrowing on page 30 shows £25m sitting in the under-12-month bucket already, with nothing filled in for any other maturity band. Which means the borrowing to arrange is not just the £34m of net additions to reach the £64m end point — it's also the £25m that reprices first. That's a lot of rolls and draws to line up against MUFG's forecast in your section 3.3 that PWLB certainty rates come down, the 5-year to 4.10% by end Q4 2027 against the 4.81% recorded at 22 December 2025.

The internal side of the same page 14 table goes the other way. Your BORROWING row — the CFR less gross debt — walks only modestly from £47.4m to £40.0m across the same five years. So most of the new capital funding comes from fresh external drawings rather than from consuming internal capacity. That's a legitimate choice given the strategy narrative on page 17 that 'medium and longer dated borrowing rates are expected to fall from their current levels', but it does concentrate more of the treasury decisions into the rate call over the next 24 to 36 months.

One small thing on affordability. Your ratio of financing costs to net revenue on page 29 has an unusual profile: 5.81, 7.30, 3.90, 5.63, 6.30 across the five years. The 2026/27 peak and 2027/28 trough are sharper than we see in most district strategies, which tend to walk smoothly. It looks driven by the £19.07m one-off net financing need in 2026/27 and the £7.45m follow-through in 2027/28 (page 8), but readers may find the 2027/28 dip is easier to explain at member briefing time with a short footnote.

And a smaller one on the liability benchmark. Your section 2.3 enumerates the four LB components verbatim from the Code but doesn't carry a printed pathway. Most district strategies in the library do print one. CIPFA's forthcoming Prudential and Treasury Code updates put the LB more centrally in front of every S151, so it may be a candidate for the next mid-year or annual outturn if not this cycle.

The page most relevant to a borrowing profile shaped like yours is pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity — every PWLB fixing daily against the DMO curve, plus the monthly breakdown of who in the sector has drawn what, at what tenor and what rate. Where you're weighing the timing of fixed-rate draws against MUFG's December forecast, seeing where the market has actually gone since is the fastest cross-check.

On training, three feel most relevant given the shape here. The liability benchmark pathway is interactive and works from live data — a natural complement to the four components already in your section 2.3. Interest rate risk, given the timing question above. And short-term vs long-term borrowing strategy, given the concentration of fixed debt in the under-12-month bucket. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts are open to the whole team.

And if any of it turns out to be useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew
